subject: geography
source_note: Topic structure follows the AQA A-Level Geography specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

topics.name: One of: Hot desert systems and landscapes / Coastal systems and landscapes / Glacial systems and landscapes
One of: Hazards / Ecosystems under stress
One of: Contemporary urban environments / Population and the environment / Resource security

connections.why: Systems thinking from the water and carbon cycles underpins how landscape systems are analysed
Cycling of water and carbon links directly to climatic hazards and ecosystem stress
Both apply physical systems to explain landscape change and environmental risk
Urban water and carbon budgets connect physical cycles to city environments
Globalisation reshapes the character and connections of local places
Global flows drive urbanisation, migration and resource demand in cities and regions
Place identity and lived experience are central to studying urban environments
Managing hazards and ecosystems increasingly relies on international governance
Place-based enquiry is a common framework for the independent investigation
Coastal and other landscape systems provide measurable fieldwork for the NEA
River and drainage-basin studies link cycle theory to primary data collection
